crab.label: Crab

source.facts: the pattern the new families follow (sea plan section 5)

crab.why: Stays (brief). The quest-ready pattern: one family, sub-types by level band, a shore kind of each zone recipe, names per slot.

frog.label: Frog

source.facts: type animal, passive in the source, walks and swims (fly_in water); no punch animation, so the port bites with its walk frames (an open question for the user)

frog.why: The one hostile family for lakes, rivers and swamp pools in every zone: today the banks hold only land mobs, and the crocodile only three swamp zones.

goby.label: Goby
goby.why: The sea's one critter fish, as the Reed Angelfish is the lakes'. Same API as our mobs (mobs_redo), MIT, so a cheap port.

source.facts: independent water spawn authority in deep-ocean columns, world slot L70

shark.label: Shark

source.facts: type monster, dogfight attack, swims (fly), has a punch animation (frames from 100)

shark.why: Rulings S12 and S13 name both: the Bay Shark (fixed L30, normal) and the Abyssal Shark (elite, open sea, next to the Kraken). World slots: one name, one level everywhere (contract item 3).

stingray.label: Stingray

source.facts: type monster, dogfight attack, swims (fly), has a punch animation (frames from 200)

stingray.why: The one hostile family of the shelf, the coastal belt, the bay rims and the channels, at zone level (channels: island level). It keeps away from the bank (S10), so nobody fights it from land.

tortoise.label: Tortoise

source.facts: type animal, not passive, has a punch animation (frames from 300), walk speed 0.2

tortoise.why: Ruling S15 names it: the neutral water beast on shores and at lakes, at zone level. Slow, so a player can always walk away.
